base_case: A confirmed three-session top (7,620 ATH on Jun 2 → relentless distribution into a -2.64% close at the low on Jun 5) has converted the topping regime into an active corrective phase. Over the next 30-60 days the base case is a controlled pullback toward the 38.2% Fib (~7,511) and the re-anchored liquidation/nervous zone (~7,240), with Monte Carlo now favoring downside-first. Trend mechanics (50d > 200d, price above both, +11.5% over 200d) remain intact, so this is a capital-preservation correction rather than a confirmed trend break — patience until a clean Fib re-entry or a reclaim above ~7,550 confirms structure.

what_changed_today: Regime arc held at Late Bull / Topping for a 4th logged session, but the topping thesis transitioned from warning to active correction.
Largest single-day loss since the April tariff shock: -200.57 pts / -2.64%, relentless sell from open to a close near the low — textbook institutional distribution.
VIX spiked from ~15 to 21.5, crossing the framework's 20-threshold; MA support now explicitly less reliable and forced-selling risk elevated.
Fear & Greed collapsed 13 points in one session (55 -> 42), flipping from Greed to Fear — the fastest deterioration of the cycle; Safe Haven downgraded two tiers to Fear.
Monte Carlo bias inverted: prob-up-first now 44.9% vs 55.1% down-first, below all regime thresholds (65/70/75) — no longer actionable on the long side.
Active leg fully retraced prior downside target; engine re-anchored downside to 7,239.85 (nervous-zone liquidation) for straddle validity.
Caution zone (~7,392, -3% from ATH) breached on a closing basis for the first time.
narrative_summary: The Late Bull / Topping regime has resolved into an active correction: SPX fell 2.64% in relentless open-to-close distribution, breaching the -3% caution zone, with Fear & Greed collapsing 13 points to Fear, VIX spiking to the 20+ risk threshold, and Monte Carlo inverting to favor downside-first (44.9% up vs 55.1% down) — below every regime action threshold. The trend mechanics remain intact (50d > 200d, price above both SMAs), so this is a capital-preservation event rather than a confirmed trend break, but valuation offers no cushion (ERP 0.26%, forward PE 20.9x). The dominant tension is an intact bull skeleton colliding with a confirmed distribution top, deteriorating sentiment/credit, and a negative quant edge. Posture is hold and monitor with defensive tripwires: no long-side action is justified, and patience for the 38.2% Fib (~7,511) or deeper re-entry zones is the default until confirmation.
open_questions: Does the 23.6% Fib (~7,553) / caution zone failure extend cleanly to the 38.2% Fib (~7,511) and the re-anchored nervous zone (~7,240), or does support hold first?
Will junk-bond spreads (4th day at April-shock ~1.45%+) tighten or sustain widening, escalating the credit warning?
Does the put/call complacency (~0.60) finally break into hedging, which would be an early bottoming tell?
Does VIX peak and reverse from the 20-25 zone to produce a high-quality re-entry signal, or stay elevated?
Can bulls reclaim ~7,550 to invalidate the confirmed top, or is 7,620 now hard resistance?

confirming_evidence: Largest single-day loss since April (-2.64%) with relentless open-to-close distribution and a close near the LOD — textbook institutional selling.
Three-session top confirmed: Jun 2 ATH -> Jun 3 distribution -> Jun 4 dead-cat -> Jun 5 breakdown acceleration.
Multi-month bearish RSI divergence on the 6-month chart has triggered; RSI broke below the 70 band and MFI rolled over.
Caution zone (~7,392, -3% from swing high) breached on a closing basis for the first time.
Monte Carlo inverted to down-first (44.9% up vs 55.1% down), below all regime thresholds — insufficient long-side edge.
Sentiment complex deteriorating broadly: F&G -13 to Fear, Safe Haven flipped to Fear, breadth in Fear, VIX above 20.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: 50d > 200d and price still above both SMAs (+7.7% vs 200d) — the bull trend skeleton is mechanically intact, arguing this is a normal dip.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Confirmed three-session distribution top, close at LOD, caution zone breached, bearish RSI divergence triggered, and VIX > 20 making MA support unreliable.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A close below the 20-day SMA after an extended advance is a regime shift, not just a normal dip; when VIX > 20, reduce confidence in MA support.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Put/call ~0.60 still complacent — no panic hedging, suggesting the move is not yet capitulative and could be shallow.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: F&G collapsed 13pts to Fear with Safe Haven flipping to Fear; complacent put/call into a falling tape means the correction likely deepens before a hedging-driven bottom.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Falling sentiment during or near new highs is a topping warning; a rising put/call from complacent levels matters more than the absolute number.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Selloff improved ERP modestly (toward ~0.26%) and forward PE eased to 20.9x as price fell.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: ERP still sits in the 0.0-0.5% valuation-ceiling band; the ERP-confirmed re-entry floor is ~7,029, far below current price — no valuation cushion to halt the decline.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: ERP 0.0-0.5% = valuation ceiling, trim bias, no aggressive adds; fundamental buyers do not step in until cushion rebuilds.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Price remains above both rising SMAs despite the pullback.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Junk demand at Extreme Fear, spread holding April-shock ~1.45% for a 4th day while breadth declines — credit and breadth both diverge from the still-elevated index.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down.

primary_tension: An intact bull-trend skeleton (50d > 200d, price above both SMAs) is colliding with a confirmed distribution top, a triggered multi-month bearish RSI divergence, sentiment/credit/breadth deterioration, VIX above the 20 risk threshold, and a Monte Carlo edge that has inverted to favor downside-first below every action threshold — defense and patience override the still-positive trend mechanics.
